name: CCS Art (Painting, Sculpture/Spatial Studies & Book Arts)
notes: Studio units required: 72 for first-year entry, 54 for sophomore transfers, 36 for junior transfers. Non-studio units required: 32 for first-year entry, 24 for sophomore transfers, 16 for junior transfers. At least 8 units of non-studio work must be completed in History of Art and Architecture Department for a letter grade or through another art history course (advisor approval needed). Up to 16 Independent Study units may apply to studio & non-studio units. Minimum 40 upper division units required. Students must complete First-Year Evaluation, Mid-Residency Review, and Senior Exhibition. All College and University requirements including CCS General Education requirements must be met.

groups.label: Studio Unit Requirements
groups.note: 72 units for students entering as first-year, 54 for sophomore transfers, 36 for junior transfers. Average 18 units of studio courses per year. Studio courses are those in which student is making art, taken in CCS or L&S Art Department. Plan to take two studio art courses per quarter.

groups.label: Non-Studio Unit Requirements
groups.note: 32 units for students entering as first-year, 24 for sophomore transfers, 16 for junior transfers. Average 8 units of non-studio art related courses per year. At least 8 units must be in History of Art and Architecture Department for a letter grade or another art history course (advisor approval needed). Non-studio courses include: Art Symposium (ART 1C), Art History courses, Art Theory courses, Visual Literacy (ART 1A), lecture portion of 7 Series (7A, 7B, 7C, 7D), and any course that informs studio practice as determined with Faculty Adviser.

groups.label: Specific L&S Art Department Course Requirements

courses.title: Visual Literacy
courses.note: Must enroll in both lecture and section for 5 units and a letter grade. Non-studio units.

courses.title: Art Symposium
courses.note: For a letter grade. Students are encouraged to take this class multiple times throughout their academic career.

subgroups.label: The 7-Series Required Course
subgroups.note: Complete the 7-Series course most aligned with your emphasis by enrolling through L&S Art Department and taking both Lecture and Section for 5 units and a letter grade. 5 units distributed as 2 non-studio units and 3 studio units. Book Arts and Painting majors enroll in 7B. Sculpture/Spatial Studies majors enroll in 7C.

courses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Practice I: Image Studies
courses.note: For Book Arts and Painting majors

courses.title: Introduction to Contemporary Practice II: Spatial Studies

subgroups.label: Additional 7-Series Courses
subgroups.note: Complete two more 7-Series courses in one of two ways: (1) Enroll in each course for full 5 units distributed as 2 non-studio and 3 studio units; OR (2) Attend lecture portion only and complete Independent Study Project Form (ART CS 199) for 1 unit - attend lecture, take notes, turn in to faculty adviser weekly.

courses.title: The Intersection of Art and Life
Introduction to Contemporary Practice I: Image Studies
Introduction to Contemporary Practice II: Spatial Studies
Introduction to Contemporary Practice III: Art, Science and Technologies

groups.label: CCS Internship/Research
groups.note: All CCS Art Majors must complete at least one 1-unit internship. Goal is to give students experience in the professional art world and related fields. Students may work or volunteer for art institution or art related business, or conduct research under instructor or graduate student. Enroll in CCS Internship/Research Project 199 or L&S Art 192 with guidance from CCS Faculty Adviser.

courses.title: CCS Internship/Research Project
courses.note: Minimum one 1-unit internship or equivalent work as determined by faculty adviser

groups.label: Evaluations, Reviews, & Exhibitions
groups.note: CCS Art Majors are required to take part in three important exhibitions/reviews: First Year Evaluation (Spring Quarter of first year - present work, artist statement, three completed physical works, PowerPoint presentation); Mid-Residency Review (arranged with faculty advisor and CCS Gallery Director - freshmen during Winter Quarter of second year but no later than Fall Quarter of third year, transfers by end of second quarter in CCS); Senior Exhibition (solo exhibition at culmination of last quarter in CCS, typically Spring quarter closest to graduation, arranged at least two quarters prior).
